name: Gera
overview: Gera was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, identified as a (grand?)son of Benjamin through his father Bela. He is listed among the sons of Israel who went to Egypt, marking him as part of the ancestral lineage that entered Egypt during the patriarchal period. His inclusion in the genealogical records highlights his place within the Benjaminite family line.
namesAndTitles: The name Gera is a proper name, possibly meaning 'sojourner.' This meaning may reflect the historical context of his family’s migration to Egypt, though the name itself was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Gera as a son of Benjamin, through Bela. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are documented in the biblical text provided.
scriptureSignificance: Gera’s significance lies in his connection to the tribe of Benjamin and his role within the broader narrative of Israel’s descent into Egypt. As a listed descendant who accompanied Israel to Egypt, he represents part of the fulfillment of God’s promises to Abraham regarding the multiplication of his descendants. His presence in the genealogical lists underscores the continuity of the Benjaminite lineage during a critical period in Israel’s history.
